rows.text: The regulation limits maximum driving time; it does not require a minimum number of driving hours.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 1 e art. 6: norme sui tempi di guida e limiti massimi

rows.text: Weekly rest is subject to minimum durations, not a maximum limit.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 4, lett. h, e art. 8, par. 6: riposi settimanali regolari e ridotti e loro minimi

rows.text: The regulation aims to improve working conditions and road safety, including by limiting driving and providing for rest.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 1 e artt. 6-8: obiettivi, limiti di guida, interruzioni e riposi

rows.text: The regulation governs driving, breaks and rest; it does not set minimum driver pay.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 1 e art. 10, par. 1: oggetto del regolamento e divieto di certe forme di pagamento, non minimo salariale

rows.text: The rules cover both goods and passenger transport, within their respective scopes.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 1 e art. 2, par. 1: trasporto di merci e passeggeri

rows.text: For goods, the general threshold is a maximum permissible mass over 3.5 tonnes, including any trailer or semi-trailer; exclusions apply.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 2, par. 1, lett. a, e art. 3: soglia e esclusioni

rows.text: The rules cover vehicles designed or adapted to carry more than nine people including the driver and intended for that purpose; exclusions apply.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 2, par. 1, lett. b, e art. 3: capacità, destinazione ed esclusioni

rows.text: The regulation applies to road transport within its scope undertaken in the EU, subject to the stated exclusions.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 2, parr. 1-2, e art. 3: campo materiale, territoriale ed esclusioni

rows.text: The territorial scope includes road transport between the EU and European Economic Area countries when the other conditions are met.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 2, parr. 1-2: campo materiale e trasporti tra Unione e SEE

rows.text: The 2025 quiz marks this FALSE: the general goods-transport threshold is over 3.5 tonnes, including a trailer. Since 1 July 2026, over 2.5 tonnes also covers certain international or cabotage operations, subject to exceptions such as qualifying own-account transport.
evidence: Regulation (EC) 561/2006 consolidated 22 May 2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf ; European Commission TRACE II guidance https://transport.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2023-12/TRACE_II_Driving-Resting_Times_Enforcement_Guidance.pdf.

Articles 2(1)(a),(aa), 3(ha): general goods threshold >3.5 t including trailers; from 1 July 2026 >2.5 t for international carriage or cabotage, subject to exceptions including qualifying own-account. Quiz source 4 April 2025, FALSO; the general-threshold reading is explanatory interpretation.

rows.text: Using a taxi or a bus alone is not enough: for passengers, vehicle capacity and purpose and any exclusions matter.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 2, par. 1, lett. b, e art. 3, lett. a: più di nove persone incluso il conducente ed esclusione di alcuni servizi regolari

rows.text: The rules concern road transport. A vehicle carried by train may be subject to specific rest rules, but that does not extend the scope to rail transport generally.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 2, par. 1, e art. 9, par. 1: trasporto su strada e riposo durante trasporto su traghetto o treno

rows.text: The scope includes certain passenger vehicles as well as goods vehicles.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 2, par. 1, lett. a e b: categorie merci e passeggeri

rows.text: The normal daily driving limit is nine hours; it may rise to ten no more than twice a week.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 6, par. 1: limite giornaliero e prolungamento

rows.text: Daily driving can reach ten hours at most twice a week; the normal limit is nine hours.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 6, par. 1: limite di nove ore e due estensioni a dieci

rows.text: Eight hours is not the maximum: the normal limit is nine hours, extendable to ten no more than twice a week.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 6, par. 1: limite giornaliero e prolungamento

rows.text: Nine hours is a normal daily driving limit, not a consecutive driving period: after four and a half hours a break is required unless a rest period begins.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 6, par. 1, e art. 7: limite giornaliero e interruzione della guida

rows.text: The normal extension permitted twice a week is to ten hours, not eleven.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 6, par. 1: limite ordinario e estensione a dieci ore

rows.text: Breaks do not authorize twelve hours of daily driving: the normal limit is nine hours, extendable to ten at most twice a week.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 6, par. 1, e art. 7: limiti giornalieri e interruzioni

rows.text: Regular daily rest comprises at least eleven hours; it can also be split into at least three hours followed by at least nine.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 4, lett. g: definizione di riposo giornaliero regolare e frazionamento

rows.text: A reduced daily rest is at least 9 but less than 11 hours. At most three are permitted between two weekly rests; that interval does not necessarily match the calendar week.
evidence: Regulation (EC) 561/2006 consolidated 22 May 2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf ; European Commission TRACE II guidance https://transport.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2023-12/TRACE_II_Driving-Resting_Times_Enforcement_Guidance.pdf.
Articles 4(g), 8(4): reduced daily rest ≥9 and <11 hours, maximum three between two weekly rests, not necessarily a calendar week. Quiz source 4 April 2025 prints VERO.

rows.text: The ordinary rule requires weekly rest to start within six consecutive 24-hour periods after the previous weekly rest ends. This is not a count of six calendar days driving; certain occasional passenger services may defer it under specific conditions.
evidence: Regulation (EC) 561/2006 consolidated 22 May 2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf ; European Commission TRACE II guidance https://transport.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2023-12/TRACE_II_Driving-Resting_Times_Enforcement_Guidance.pdf.

Articles 8(6),(6a): ordinary weekly rest starts no later than six 24-hour periods after the previous weekly rest ends; conditions apply to up-to-12-period occasional passenger service derogation. Quiz source 4 April 2025 prints VERO as shorthand.

rows.text: The limit of three reduced daily rests is counted between two weekly rest periods, not simply by calendar week.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 8, par. 4: massimo tre riposi giornalieri ridotti tra due riposi settimanali

rows.text: The quiz marks this FALSE, treating 9 hours alone as insufficient for a regular daily rest. Regular rest is at least 11 consecutive hours, or split into at least 3 hours followed by at least 9; 9 to under 11 consecutive hours is reduced rest.
evidence: Regulation (EC) 561/2006 consolidated 22 May 2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf ; European Commission TRACE II guidance https://transport.ec.europa.eu/system/files/2023-12/TRACE_II_Driving-Resting_Times_Enforcement_Guidance.pdf.

Article 4(g): regular daily rest ≥11 continuous hours or ≥3 followed by ≥9; reduced is ≥9 and <11. Quiz source 4 April 2025 prints FALSO; treating 9 hours as sufficient is an explanatory interpretation; 11 hours also satisfies “at least 9”.

rows.text: Daily rest has its own durations: regular rest is at least eleven hours, while reduced rest is at least nine and less than eleven. It need not equal driving time.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) n. 561/2006, testo consolidato 31.12.2024, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-12-31/eng — art. 4, lett. g, e art. 6, par. 1: definizioni del riposo giornaliero e limite della guida

issues.reason: Il quiz stampa FALSO per la soglia superiore a 2,5 t senza precisare il tipo di trasporto; dal 1 luglio 2026 tale soglia si applica almeno ai trasporti internazionali o di cabotaggio. Non è chiaro se si debba interpretare la frase come regola generale esclusiva, malgrado il diverso trattamento della soglia di 3,5 t nel quesito 27537.
checked_sources: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A02006R0561-20241231 art. 2(1)(a) e (aa): oltre 3,5 t in generale e oltre 2,5 t in trasporti internazionali o cabotaggio dal 1 luglio 2026; art. 3 elenca esclusioni.

issues.reason: Il quiz stampa VERO per non più di tre riposi ridotti per settimana, ma la norma conta i tre riposi tra due riposi settimanali e definisce la settimana da lunedì a domenica; i due intervalli non coincidono necessariamente.
checked_sources: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A02006R0561-20241231 artt. 4(g), 4(i) e 8(4): riposo ridotto almeno 9 e meno di 11 ore, settimana lunedì-domenica, massimo tre riduzioni tra due riposi settimanali.

issues.reason: Il quiz stampa VERO per un divieto assoluto di guidare oltre sei giorni consecutivi; la regola effettiva riguarda sei periodi di 24 ore tra riposi settimanali e ammette una deroga per servizi occasionali di passeggeri.
checked_sources: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A02006R0561-20241231 art. 8(6) e (6a): inizio del riposo entro sei periodi di 24 ore e possibile rinvio fino a dodici a condizioni specifiche.
https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A52014DC0337: la Commissione descrive la deroga al riposo settimanale come regola dei 12 giorni.

issues.reason: Il quiz stampa FALSO per «almeno nove ore», ma il minimo di undici ore del riposo regolare soddisfa letteralmente anche il limite inferiore di nove; non è chiaro se sia inteso come minimo sufficiente di nove ore.
checked_sources: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX%3A02006R0561-20241231 art. 4(g): riposo giornaliero regolare almeno 11 ore, alternativamente frazionato 3 più 9; ridotto almeno 9 e meno di 11.
